How to generate a RESTful API request on Cisco Nexus Dashboard?
Version: 6.3.1
IP: 192.120.45.67
API name: get information of an interface
Parameter_fabricName: Network1
Parameter_nodeId: 12
Parameter_podId: 10
Parameter_interfaceType: Ethernet
Parameter_infoType: Speed

function.name: requests_get
function.description: Send a GET request to retrieve specified information for an interface from a network telemetry API. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL endpoint to send the GET request to. This should include the base path without query parameters, e.g., 'https://{ip}/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/interfaceInfo'.

params.description: The query parameters for the request.

fabricName.description: The name of the fabric to limit nodes pertaining to.

nodeId.description: The node identifier to limit results pertaining to.

podId.description: The pod identifier to limit results pertaining to.

interfaceType.description: The type of the interface to limit results pertaining to.

infoType.description: The type of information requested for the interface.

Below is a step‑by‑step guide to build and fire a **RESTful GET** request against the Cisco Nexus Dashboard (ND) API that returns the *Speed* information for a specific interface. | Item | Value | |------|-------| | **Base URL** | `https://192.120.45.67` | | **Endpoint** | `/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/interfaceInfo` | | **HTTP Method** | `GET` | | **Query Parameters** | `fabricName=Network1`
`nodeId=12`
`podId=10`
`interfaceType=ethernet`
`infoType=Speed` | | **Authentication** | ND uses **Basic Auth** (username/password) or a **Bearer token**. Replace `` and `` or `` accordingly. | | **Headers** | `Accept: application/json`
`Content-Type: application/json` | --- ## 1. Build the full URL ```text https://192.120.45.67/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/interfaceInfo?fabricName=Network1&nodeId=12&podId=10&interfaceType=ethernet&infoType=Speed ``` > **Tip:** > * `interfaceType` is case‑sensitive – use the lower‑case value `"ethernet"` as shown. > * If you want to query multiple nodes or pods, simply add more `nodeId`/`podId` parameters (comma‑separated or repeated). --- ## 2. Example `curl` command ```bash curl -k \ -u : \ # Basic Auth -H "Accept: application/json" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ "https://192.120.45.67/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/interfaceInfo?fabricName=Network1&nodeId=12&podId=10&interfaceType=ethernet&infoType=Speed" ``` *Replace `` and `` with your ND credentials.* If you’re using a bearer token: ```bash curl -k \ -H "Authorization: Bearer " \ -H "Accept: application/json" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ "https://192.120.45.67/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/interfaceInfo?fabricName=Network1&nodeId=12&podId=10&interfaceType=ethernet&infoType=Speed" ``` --- ## 3. Using the provided `requests_get` helper If you prefer to call the helper function directly (Python‑style), here’s how: ```python from functions import requests_get response = requests_get( url="https://192.120.45.67/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/interfaceInfo", params={ "fabricName": "Network1", "nodeId": 12, "podId": 10, "interfaceType": "ethernet", "infoType": "Speed" } ) print(response) # <-- JSON payload with the interface speed ``` > **Note:** > The helper will automatically handle the HTTP GET, query‑string encoding, and return the parsed JSON (or raw response if you prefer). --- ## 4. Sample Response A successful call typically returns something like: ```json { "fabricName": "Network1", "nodeId": 12, "podId": 10, "interfaceType": "ethernet", "infoType": "Speed", "data": { "interface": "Ethernet1/1", "speed": "1000Mbps" } } ``` If the interface isn’t found or the parameters are wrong, you’ll receive an error object (e.g., 404 or 400) with a descriptive message. --- ### Quick Checklist | ✅ | Item | |----|------| | ✅ | Correct base URL (`https://`) | | ✅ | Endpoint path (`/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/interfaceInfo`) | | ✅ | Query parameters match the API spec | | ✅ | Authentication header (Basic or Bearer) | | ✅ | `Accept: application/json` header | | ✅ | Use `-k` or `--insecure` only if you’re okay with self‑signed certs; otherwise, install the proper CA cert. | That’s all you need to pull the *Speed* of an interface from Cisco Nexus Dashboard 6.3.1. Happy querying!
